# Live wounded soldiers and terminal death

The previous `soldier_death.gsc::try_long_death` selected crawling/back animations after the retained damage code had already reduced health to zero and notified death. `ActorDie` disabled damage, Survival counted the kill and the native death frame changed collision/corpse ownership. The visual appeared wounded while the engine correctly regarded that entity as dead.

IW4 `animscripts/pain.gsc::crawlingPain` (620 onward) instead enters its wounded sequence while health is positive and no greater than100. Its eventual `killWrapper` (1281) performs a real kill attributed to the last damaging player. T5 `G_DamageActor` similarly distinguishes a damageable live actor from a dead one. The port now follows that lifecycle: low-positive-health infantry pain may enter the existing authored crawl/back sequence; an initially lethal hit remains lethal. No dead actor is revived, no incoming damage is capped and no magazine/health is refilled.

The native begin method validates the live soldier, actual pain state, positive remaining health below40%/at most100, damageability and absence of ride/traversal/scripted ownership. It releases cover and holds combat routing while the existing animation/root motion runs. It preserves the actual health, eType18, sentient team, solid/body collision and damage reception. Another shot reaches ordinary retained `G_Damage`. Natural sequence completion applies the remaining health through the same native damage path, using the last damaging entity only if its native useCount generation still matches. The real death handler clears wounded state once; the death script then chooses the appropriate grounded terminal clip. Interrupted or refused damage never fabricates a death/reward. Existing actor allocation/reset/corpse ownership contains the state, with no detached timer or archive substitution.

The shared Windows EXE and host DLL build passed. Production-body ASan/UBSan tests cover low-health admission/refusal, unchanged live identity/collision, subsequent damage, one final death, bleedout attribution/generation, invalid receivers and interruption cleanup. Actual GSC crawl/back tests execute `living_enemies` and `death_watch` to verify no early count removal/reward and exactly one final kill. The native crosshair regression retains enemy classification at1HP; C1 actor team/history and magazine/drop regressions still pass. Generic-human animation parity remains identical1058entries. All four category closures pass against the final built EXE.

Owned Favela UDP17761 wave7 PID41060 observed actor818 naturally enter `wounded (crawl)` with HP10, alive1, six living enemies and zero wave/player kills. One real finishing shot produced HP0, alive0, five living enemies, exactly one wave kill and one player kill. The other five enemies were then killed; six spawned/six killed/zero failures and ten seconds of death observation completed without a script runtime error. The owned process quit and the port was released. No user process, deployed server, UI or C1 input was changed. This is native lifecycle proof, not C1 visual acceptance. Exact source/binary hashes, logs and diagnostic-only staged GSC are retained in `docs/releases/actor-wounded-live-probe-20261029.json`.

The initial owned wave7 run exposed another real bug: death during `react_to_grenade` canceled that helper, but move/combat/stop owning behavior roots lacked a death endon and could evaluate its undefined result. Those root frames now end on death before evaluating or resuming movement; existing killanimscript ownership remains. This is cancellation, not coercion of an unknown result to false. The actual caller regression reproduces the old failure and verifies root cancellation; the final native wave7 kill-all/death observation was clean.

Final rawfiles source: `f05ed0ccb1261d9334cdd52738f5816f02e668ee`. The native production delta is committed with this receipt; its exact tested file hashes and shared build identities are recorded there. Installation is tracked separately in the local deployment manifest.
